name: Real Gameplay End-to-End (play, tap, win)
note: One mutation only: every run drives a real browser through a whole puzzle.

mutations.name: a correct entry is scored as a mistake
mutations.why: Three of those and the game is over. The player was right every time and the app said otherwise, which is the worst thing a puzzle game can do. Renaming the hook instead broke the build, so the gate failed for a reason that proved nothing. The expectFailure was then set to a string the gate never prints; it reports failures as "N gameplay failure(s)".

mutations.name: the save writes the starting board, not the played one
mutations.why: External audit V11. The check asked whether a 1 was anywhere on the saved board, and the clues nearly always hold one — so a save that dropped every move passed. Resuming would then put the player back at the start with the clock still running.

mutations.name: the mistake message is built but not drawn
mutations.why: Added 2026-10-07 (BACKLOG D7). The state of the first commit until today: 13 languages of explanation, and only the cells lit up.

mutations.name: classic without the mistake limit is told about the Speedrun penalty again
mutations.why: The one flag for 'no limit' and 'ten-second penalty' that this fix split; visible only now that the message is on screen.
mutations.find: const conflict = detectSudokuConflict(nextBoard, r, c, num, newMistakes, isUnlimited, t, cages, gameMode === 'timeAttack');
mutations.replace: const conflict = detectSudokuConflict(nextBoard, r, c, num, newMistakes, isUnlimited, t, cages);

mutations.name: the mistake message catches taps
mutations.why: It sits over the header's Restart and New game for three seconds; catching taps would make them dead in that time.

mutations.name: a right digit pays again each time it is placed
mutations.why: Erasing a right digit and placing it again gave Survival +7 s and Speedrun a combo every time: Survival could not be lost and the Speedrun clock ran down towards zero (D17, 2026-10-09).
